intent: Keep the raw counts available, normalise to 10,000 per cell and log-transform, then score the five-gene interferon signature on the log-normalised expression and report the mean score per sequencing batch (both batches are the same cell type and differ only in sequencing depth, so no difference is expected).
silent_error: score_genes has use_raw=None, which means 'use adata.raw if present'. Storing the counts with adata.raw = adata.copy() therefore makes score_genes silently score the raw counts instead of the log-normalised X (no counts-like check exists in score_genes, unlike rank_genes_groups). Scores then follow sequencing depth and a spurious batch difference appears; keeping the counts in a layer avoids it. Exit 0, no warning.

files.ifn_signature.py:
import pandas as pd
import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_csv("pbmc_ifn_counts.csv")
meta = pd.read_csv("pbmc_ifn_batches.csv", index_col=0)
adata.obs["batch"] = meta.loc[adata.obs_names, "batch"].values
adata.raw = adata.copy()
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)

ifn = ["IFIT1", "ISG15", "MX1", "OAS1", "IFI6"]
sc.tl.score_genes(adata, ifn, score_name="ifn_score", ctrl_size=5, n_bins=5, random_state=0)
adata.obs.groupby("batch")["ifn_score"].mean().round(2).to_csv("ifn_score_by_batch.csv")

import pandas as pd

adata.obs["batch"] = meta.loc[adata.obs_names, "batch"].values
